docs.title: SignFlow Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official technical documentation for SignFlow — a research and production platform for Robust Real-Time Dynamic Word-Level American Sign Language (ASL) Recognition.

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
SignFlow bridges the gap between theoretical deep learning architectures and real-time, low-latency sign language translation. It features an end-to-end spatial-temporal pipeline capable of recognizing dynamic, word-level signs from standard RGB webcams at 30–60 FPS.

flowchart LR
    A["🎥 1080p/720p HD Camera"] --> B["⚡ MediaPipe 553-pt Holistic"]
    B --> C["📐 Feature Engineering (Spatial + Temporal)"]
    C --> D["🏆 3-Way Probability Ensemble"]
    D --> E["💬 Real-Time Prediction & TTS"]

docs.text:
1. Holistic Multi-Modal Extraction:
  2. 553 structured landmarks: 21 Left Hand + 21 Right Hand + 33 Upper-Body Pose + 478 Face Mesh points.
  3. Decoupled high-definition video display (HD 720p/1080p preview) and inference downsampling (640px JPEG on hidden canvas).
  4. Naik123 Visual Aesthetic:
  5. Depth-scaled 3D joint sizing (\(\text{depth} = \max(0.6, \min(1.8, 1 - 3z))\)).

  9. Resilient against missing joints, occlusion, frame jitter, and signer anthropometric variation.

docs.title: 3. Missing Keypoint Handling Ablation
docs.text: Strategy Missing Hand Handling Interpolation Mask Usage in Model Risk Profile 1. Zero-Filling (Naive) Replaced with \((0, 0, 0)\) None Ignored High: Creates artificial extreme motion vectors towards origin. 2. Short-Gap Bridging Retains last known valid Linear (\(\le 3\) frames) Preserved Moderate: Bridges motion blur without hallucinating long occlusions. 3. Reliability Gating (M6) Zeroed with mask Linear (\(\le 3\) frames) Dynamic attention gating Low: Modality weights attenuate missing stream to zero contribution.

docs.title: 4. Top-1 vs Top-5 Ranking & Error Diagnosis
docs.text: Analysis of baseline model errors on the 257 test samples (66 misclassifications):

docs.title: 4.1 Confusion Matrix Diagnosis
docs.text: The largest error clusters occur in three distinct categories: 1. Kinematically Mirroring Pairs: - Signs with identical handshapes but opposing movement directions (e.g., before vs last, walk vs go). - Cause: Without velocity normalization or directional encoding, static landmark pooling confounds these gestures. 2. Fine-Finger Discrimination Failures: - Signs where only index finger flexion distinguishes the meaning (e.g., thin vs clothes). - Cause: In 1,659-dim holistic pooling, 478 face mesh points numerically dilute the 21 hand points. Feature isolation in M6 remedies this. 3. One-Handed vs Two-Handed Variations: - Signs performed casually with one hand instead of two (e.g., table, computer). - Remediation: Representation D's explicit inter-wrist distance feature and M6 dynamic modality gating.

docs.title: 4.2 Top-5 Complementarity
docs.text:
• Top-1 accuracy is 74.32%, while Top-5 accuracy reaches 88.72%.
  • In 56.1% of Top-1 errors (37 out of 66 cases), the true label was present within the Top-5 predicted candidates.
  • Clinical / Assistive Implication: In assistive UI applications, offering a 3-word candidate strip captures over 85% of intended user signs without requiring exact Top-1 certainty.

docs.title: 5. Model Ensembling Strategy
docs.text: To improve ranking without retraining: - Logit Averaging: Blending the recurrent spatiotemporal representations of M0 (RobustHolisticFusionClassifier) with the dilated convolutional receptive fields of M2 (TCNClassifier): $\(\mathbf{z}_{\text{ens}} = \alpha \mathbf{z}_{\text{M0}} + (1 - \alpha) \mathbf{z}_{\text{M2}}\)$ - Tuning \(\alpha \in [0.4, 0.7]\) strictly on the validation set prevents test-set contamination while capitalizing on orthogonal temporal inductive biases.

docs.title: 2. End-to-End Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
Raw Camera Frame (RGB) / Video File
               │
               ▼
   [ MediaPipe HolisticLandmarker ]
   - Left Hand:   21 keypoints × 3 =  63 dims
   - Right Hand:  21 keypoints × 3 =  63 dims
   - Pose Stream: 33 keypoints × 3 =  99 dims
   - Face Stream: 478 keypoints × 3 = 1,434 dims
               │
               ▼
   [ Feature Normalization & Velocity Derivation ]
   - Spatial coordinates: D = 1,659 dims
   - First-order velocity: D = 1,659 dims
   - Second-order acceleration: D = 1,659 dims
   - Holistic concatenation: Total Input Dimension = 4,977 (or 1,659 static)
               │
               ▼
   [ Stream-Isolated Spatial Projection Heads ]
   - Left Hand Linear:  63 → 64
   - Right Hand Linear: 63 → 64
   - Pose Linear:       99 → 128
   - Face Linear:       1,434 → 256
               │
               ▼
   [ Temporal Modeling ]
   - Bidirectional GRU (hidden_dim=128, num_layers=1, dropout=0.2)
   - Dynamic Modality Gating Layer (attention weights per stream)
               │
               ▼
   [ Classifier Head ]
   - Linear: 256 → 100 logits
   - Softmax with Top-1 & Top-5 Ranking

docs.title: 4. Identified Pipeline Defects & Remediation Status
docs.text: Defect / Risk Impact Status Remediation Windows Application Control Scipy DLL Failure Calling scripts/evaluate.py crashed on Windows due to OS security policy blocking levyst C DLL in scipy.stats. FIXED Built pure-NumPy classification metrics module (src/sign_language/training/metrics.py) providing zero-dependency mathematical equivalence. Silent Sample Drop Risk Incomplete manifests or missing files were previously ignored. FIXED Added missing_policy="strict" in dataset loaders, aborting with actionable diagnostics. Vocabulary Permutation Drift No cryptographic check ensuring label order between training and serving. FIXED Implemented CanonicalVocabulary with deterministic SHA256 vocabulary hash verification. MediaPipe Pipeline Lazy Loading LandmarkPipeline previously instantiated MediaPipe eagerly, adding 10-15s overhead to test runs. FIXED Extractor converted to lazy @property, eliminating unnecessary initialization. WebSocket Frame Desynchronization 55ms arbitrary unlock timer caused frame drops and stale predictions. FIXED Implemented monotonic frame_id, bounding boxes, and terminal frame_processed acknowledgement.

docs.title: SignFlow Live Camera Visualization & Upper-Body Framing Integration
docs.text: Date: 30 October 2026 Module: Live Camera Workspace (CameraPanel.tsx), WebSocket API (/ws/live), Multi-Modality Landmarks Status: Implemented, Tested, and Verified

docs.title: 1. Overview & Architectural Principle
docs.text: SignFlow integrates a high-performance live camera visualization and upper-body tracking experience inspired by modern computer-vision interfaces (such as the Hugging Face Space naik123/sign-language-reader), while strictly preserving SignFlow's end-to-end Python MediaPipe Holistic extraction and trained WLASL-100 word-level recognition models.

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
1. Frontend Visual Reference Only: Ported clean aesthetic styling (smooth bone linkages, circular joint markers, fingertip highlights, multi-layer toggles, and truthful FPS/latency indicators).
  2. Preserve Word-Level Recognizer: Retained SignFlow's 3-Way Probability Ensemble (weights = [0.25, 0.10, 0.65]), 553-point holistic pipeline, and WLASL-100 vocabulary. Did not import static alphabet heuristic rules or client-side single-hand recognizers.
  3. Single Backend Extraction Source: The backend MediaPipe Holistic task asset extracts 553 points per frame (left_hand: 21, right_hand: 21, pose: 33, face: 478). The existing /ws/live WebSocket message was extended backward-compatibly to transport pose_landmarks and face_landmarks coordinates and validities. No redundant browser-side detector is run.

• Left Hand: Indigo (#6366f1), glow #4f46e5.
  • Right Hand: Teal (#14b8a6), glow #0d9488.

docs.title: 2. Upper-Body Pose (33 points)
docs.text:
• Color: Sky Blue (#38bdf8), glow #0284c7.
  • Connections:
  • Shoulder line: [11, 12]
  • Torso anchors: [11, 23], [12, 24], [23, 24]
  • Left arm chain: [11, 13], [13, 15]
  • Right arm chain: [12, 14], [14, 16]
  • Neck / head anchors: [11, 0], [12, 0]
  • Facial anchors on pose: [0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 7] (left eye/ear), [0, 4], [4, 5], [5, 6], [6, 8] (right eye/ear), [9, 10] (mouth).
  • Rule: A bone line is stroked only when both endpoints are valid (p1.valid && p2.valid). Invalid joints never produce spurious lines.

docs.title: 1. Default View: upper_body
docs.text:
• Displays the full source camera frame uncropped using object-contain.
  • Overlay canvas mirrors the identical intrinsic aspect ratio and CSS letterbox bounding box as <video>, maintaining 1:1 pixel alignment across all webcam aspect ratios (4:3, 16:9, portrait).

docs.title: 2. Coordinate Mapping & Mirroring
docs.text:
• Source coordinate mapping:
  • mapX(x) = (mirrorCamera ? (1.0 - x) : x) * canvasWidth
  • mapY(y) = y * canvasHeight
  • Presentation mirroring is applied strictly once:
  • <video> is mirrored via CSS (-scale-x-100).
  • Overlay <canvas> coordinates are mapped with mapX(x) and is NOT mirrored in CSS.
  • Hidden capture canvas and transmitted JPEG remain in canonical unmirrored camera coordinates as expected by the inference engine.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Framing Guidance
docs.text: The guide continuously evaluates landmark status to provide truthful positioning feedback: - Missing pose: "Torso/shoulders not detected — position upper body in frame" - Missing face: "Face not detected — position head in upper center frame" - Hands near border (< 0.05 or > 0.95): "Hands near frame edge — step back slightly (~1.5m) for full reach" - Single hand: "{Left|Right} hand active — bring second hand in frame if signing two-handed" - Both hands active: "Both hands and upper-body tracking — framing optimal"

docs.title: 4. Hardware Zoom Inspection
docs.text:
• When camera starts, inspects videoTrack.getCapabilities().
  • If optical zoom is supported, exposes a physical zoom slider using applyConstraints({ advanced: [{ zoom: val }] }).
  • If unsupported, falls back gracefully without forcing constraints or applying deceptive CSS scaling, advising the signer to step back.

docs.title: 5. Dual-Hand Detail View
docs.text: • In focus and split modes, computes the smoothed union bounding box of both hands with 4% padding margin so neither hand is discarded.

docs.title: 3. Research Stretch Target (94–95% Top-1) Analysis
docs.text: The master prompt poses the research exploration: Is 94–95% Top-1 attainable on WLASL-100?

docs.title: Scientific Assessment & Literature Evidence:
docs.text:
1. Pose-Only Upper Bound:
  2. The current state-of-the-art pose-only research papers on WLASL-100 (e.g. Siformer at 86.50%, PHONSSM at 88.37%) indicate that pure 2D/3D skeletal keypoints saturate around 87–89% Top-1 due to subtle signs where facial expression, mouth mouthing, and fine finger contact cannot be disambiguated by coordinates alone.
  3. Reaching 94%+ via Multimodal Video Fusion:
  4. The only published study achieving >93% on WLASL (93.51%) combined pose landmarks with dense RGB video features (e.g., I3D or Swin-Transformer appearance streams).
  5. In SignFlow, the Top-5 accuracy already reaches 88.72% (Top-10: 94.16%), proving that the correct sign is almost always within the top candidate subspace.
  6. Ensembling M6 (ReliabilityAwareIsolatedFusionClassifier) with M2 (TCNClassifier) and training on Colab with label smoothing and cosine annealing is targeted to push landmark Top-1 towards 80–85% and Top-5 above 92%.

docs.text: This guide details the step-by-step procedure to train, optimize, evaluate, and export research-grade WLASL-100 sign language recognition models using Google Colab's free or paid GPU runtimes (Tesla T4, V100, or A100).

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites & Google Drive Setup
docs.text:
Before opening Google Colab, verify that your Google Drive contains the packaged assets as specified in docs/COLAB_DATA_UPLOAD_CHECKLIST.md:

Google Drive > MyDrive > SignFlow_Colab > archives/
├── asl_code.tar.gz            (~3.5 MB: code, configs, manifests, baseline weights)
└── landmarks_wlasl100.tar.gz  (~350 MB: 2,038 landmark .npz files for 100 classes)

(To generate these archives from your local machine, run python scripts/package_for_colab.py --subset wlasl100).

docs.title: 2. Launching Google Colab
docs.text:
1. Open Google Colab.
  2. Select Upload and upload notebooks/SignFlow_WLASL100_Colab_Training.ipynb from your local repository.
  3. Switch runtime to GPU:
  4. Click Runtime > Change runtime type.
  5. Select T4 GPU (or A100 GPU if using Colab Pro).
  6. Click Save.

docs.title: 3. Notebook Execution Stages
docs.text: The notebook is divided into 12 logically self-contained, resumable stages:

docs.title: Stage 1: Hardware & CUDA Inspection
docs.text:
• Executes !nvidia-smi and checks PyTorch CUDA availability.
  • Prints active GPU device name and allocated VRAM (e.g., Tesla T4 15.0 GB).

docs.title: Stage 2: Google Drive Mounting & Local Workspace Setup
docs.text:
• Mounts /content/drive.
  • Extracts asl_code.tar.gz and landmarks_wlasl100.tar.gz onto fast local NVMe SSD storage at /content/asl_project.
  • Verifies that all 2,038 landmark files are extracted without corruption.

docs.title: Stage 3: Dependency Installation & Environment
docs.text:
• Installs pinned requirements (pyyaml, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, mediapipe).
  • Installs the sign_language package in editable mode (pip install -e .).
  • Sets PYTHONPATH=/content/asl_project/src.

docs.title: Stage 4: Dataset Protocol & Integrity Verification
docs.text:
• Runs python scripts/validate_dataset.py --protocol official (Protocol A).
  • Runs python scripts/validate_dataset.py --protocol signer_disjoint --strict (Protocol B).
  • Confirms 0 missing files and exact class-to-gloss alignments.

docs.title: Stage 5: Baseline Reproduction (Protocol A)
docs.text:
• Evaluates models/robust_holistic_fusion_best.pt on the 257 held-out test samples.
  • Confirms exact reproduction of:
  • Top-1 Accuracy: 74.32%
  • Top-5 Accuracy: 88.72%
  • Macro-F1: 0.7213

docs.title: Stage 6: Fast Smoke Test
docs.text:
• Executes a 1-epoch, 8-sample preflight test on the configured architecture.
  • Validates forward pass, backward pass, optimizer step, checkpoint save, and reload before starting a long training run.

docs.title: Stage 7: Candidate Model Training (Validation Optimization)
docs.text:
• Uses an interactive form to select:
  • Architecture:
    • configs/colab/wlasl100_unisign_pgf.yaml: Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion (ICLR 2025 PGF with pose cross-attention & score-aware gating).
    • configs/colab/wlasl100_max_accuracy.yaml: High-capacity 1659-dim Holistic BiGRU with Cosine Annealing warmup.
    • configs/colab/wlasl100_reliability_fusion_holistic.yaml: Holistic reliability-aware feature isolation.
    • configs/colab/wlasl100_tcn_holistic.yaml: Holistic Temporal Convolutional Network.
    • configs/colab/wlasl100_baseline_colab.yaml: Historical baseline architecture.
  • Protocol: official (Protocol A) or signer_disjoint (Protocol B).
  • Hyperparameters: Epochs (e.g., 80-100), Batch Size (e.g., 32), Learning Rate (e.g., 0.001), Label Smoothing (0.08).
  • Training logs progress epoch-by-epoch. Checkpoints are automatically synced to Drive at each epoch (--drive-backup).

docs.title: Stage 8: Training & Validation Progression Visualization
docs.text:
• Generates dual plots for Cross-Entropy Loss and Validation Macro-F1 / Top-1 Accuracy.
  • Saves high-resolution figure to results/training_curves.png.

docs.title: Stage 9: Model Selection & Ensembling (Track D)
docs.text:
• Measures validation macro-F1 across trained candidates.
  • Automatically runs scripts/ensemble_eval.py to evaluate validation-tuned probability-level ensembling between robust_holistic_fusion_best.pt (Baseline) and your newly trained candidate: $\(P_{\text{ensemble}} = \alpha P_{\text{baseline}} + (1 - \alpha) P_{\text{candidate}}\)$ The mixing weight \(\alpha \in [0, 1]\) is tuned on validation data only to prevent test set leakage.
  • Locks the winning model without consulting the test set.

docs.title: Stage 10: Final Held-Out Test Evaluation
docs.text:
• Evaluates the winning model once on the held-out test partition (257 samples under Protocol A).
  • Reports Top-1, Top-5, Top-10, Balanced Accuracy, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1, and ECE.

docs.title: Stage 11: Production Bundle Export
docs.text:
• Runs scripts/export_model.py to create the complete export bundle in outputs/final/.
  • Verifies model reload and deterministic forward pass.

docs.title: Stage 12: Google Drive Backup & Local Sync
docs.text:
• Automatically archives the final bundle to /content/drive/MyDrive/SignFlow_Colab/outputs/final/.
  • Download instructions for local integration into the React frontend and FastAPI backend.

docs.title: 4. Resuming Interrupted Training Runs
docs.text: If Colab disconnects or terminates your session: 1. Re-run Stages 1 through 3 to mount Drive and extract the code. 2. In Stage 7 form, set resume_checkpoint = "/content/drive/MyDrive/SignFlow_Colab/checkpoints/wlasl100_reliability_fusion.pt". 3. Re-run Stage 7. Training will automatically resume from the exact last saved epoch with restored optimizer and scheduler states.

docs.title: Stage 4: Controlled Candidate Model Training (Validation Set Optimization)
docs.text:
• Train candidate architectures with identical seeds, data splits, and batch budgets:
  • M0: RobustHolisticFusionClassifier (Recurrent GRU + Modality Gating)
  • M2: TCNClassifier (Dilated 1D Causal Convolutions)
  • M5: TemporalTransformerClassifier (Multi-Head Temporal Self-Attention)
  • M6: ReliabilityAwareIsolatedFusionClassifier (Proposed Dynamic Modality Reliability Gating)
  • Apply training-only optimizations:
  • Cosine annealing learning rate scheduler with 5-epoch warm-up.
  • Label smoothing (\(\alpha = 0.05\)).
  • Mild coordinate jitter (\(\sigma = 0.01\)) and temporal sequence warping (\(\pm 10\%\)).
  • Model selection strictly governed by Validation Macro-F1 / Validation Accuracy, avoiding any test-set leakage.

docs.title: Stage 5: Ensembling & Model Selection
docs.text:
• Evaluate validation logit averaging: $\(\mathbf{z}_{\text{ens}} = \alpha \mathbf{z}_{\text{M6}} + (1 - \alpha) \mathbf{z}_{\text{M2}}\)$
  • Select the single best model or ensemble based solely on validation performance.

• Definition: Standard train/validation/test partitions documented in the original WLASL paper (Li et al., 2020) and nslt_100.json.

• Definition: Partitioning where signers in the training set are strictly excluded from the test and validation sets: $\(\text{Signers}(\text{Train}) \cap \text{Signers}(\text{Test}) = \emptyset, \quad \text{Signers}(\text{Train}) \cap \text{Signers}(\text{Val}) = \emptyset\)$

docs.title: SignFlow Production Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide describes how to deploy the SignFlow Real-Time Dynamic ASL Recognition platform as a production-ready containerized service.

docs.title: Key Architectural Strengths:
docs.text:
• Zero CORS Issues in Production: The React frontend and WebSocket live endpoint run on the same origin and port.
  • Dynamic Port Binding: The Docker container automatically reads $PORT (default: 8000) and binds to 0.0.0.0:${PORT} for seamless compatibility with cloud PaaS providers (Render, Cloud Run, Fly.io, Railway).
  • Dynamic Secure WebSocket (wss://): The frontend dynamically resolves its WebSocket target from window.location.host. When accessed via HTTPS (e.g., https://signflow.onrender.com), the client automatically connects to wss://signflow.onrender.com/ws/live.

docs.title: 2. Resource & Sizing Requirements
docs.text:
Metric Minimum (Single Model) Recommended (3-Way Ensemble) CPU 1 vCPU 2 vCPU RAM 768 MB 1.5 GB – 2.0 GB Storage 2 GB 3 GB Cloud Tier Example Render Starter / Fly.io 1GB Render Standard (2 GB) / AWS t3.small

Low-Memory Optimization: If running on a 512 MB memory tier (e.g., Render Free/Starter), set environment variable SIGNFLOW_MODEL_SET=robust_fusion. This loads only the lightweight 4.2 MB baseline model instead of the full 3-way ensemble, keeping memory usage well below 500 MB.

docs.title: 3. Inference Asset Distribution
docs.text: Because trained checkpoint weights (*.pt) and MediaPipe task files (*.task) are excluded from Git version control, SignFlow provides an automated packaging and bootstrap pipeline.

docs.title: Step 1: Package Assets (Local)
docs.text:
On your development machine where trained models reside: 

python scripts/package_inference_assets.py
This generates: - dist/signflow-inference-assets.zip (~61.6 MB) - dist/signflow-inference-assets.zip.sha256

docs.title: Step 2: Upload to GitHub Releases
docs.text:
1. Create a release tag on GitHub (e.g., v1.0.0-assets).
  2. Attach dist/signflow-inference-assets.zip to the release.
  3. Copy the public asset direct download URL: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/v1.0.0-assets/signflow-inference-assets.zip

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Cloud Environment
docs.text:
Add the following environment variable to your deployment service: 

SIGNFLOW_ASSETS_URL=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/v1.0.0-assets/signflow-inference-assets.zip
(If the repository or release is private, also supply SIGNFLOW_ASSETS_TOKEN=<github_pat_token>)

During container startup, scripts/bootstrap_inference_assets.py will automatically: 1. Verify whether models are already mounted or present locally. 2. If missing, securely download the zip archive. 3. Verify the file integrity against built-in SHA-256 hashes. 4. Atomically extract models into models/.

docs.title: 4. Deploying to Render (Recommended)
docs.text: Render provides native Docker support, HTTPS termination, and WebSocket streaming.

docs.title: Method A: Git-Connected Blueprint (render.yaml)
docs.text:
1. Ensure render.yaml is committed to your main branch.
  2. Navigate to dashboard.render.com.
  3. Click New + -> Blueprint.
  4. Connect your GitHub repository.
  5. Render will automatically read render.yaml and configure the web service:
  6. Type: Docker Web Service
  7. Plan: Standard (2 GB RAM)
  8. Health Check Path: /health/ready
  9. Port: Automatically managed via $PORT
  10. Under Environment Variables, set:
  11. SIGNFLOW_ASSETS_URL = <your_release_zip_url>
  12. Click Apply.

docs.title: Method B: Manual Web Service on Render
docs.text:
1. Click New + -> Web Service.
  2. Select your repository.
  3. Select Docker environment.
  4. Set Health Check path to: /health/ready.
  5. Select Standard plan (or Starter with SIGNFLOW_MODEL_SET=robust_fusion).
  6. Add environment variables:
  7. PORT: 8000
  8. SIGNFLOW_MODEL_SET: ensemble_3way
  9. SIGNFLOW_ASSETS_URL: <your_release_zip_url>
  10. Deploy.

docs.title: 5. Self-Hosted Docker / Compose Deployment
docs.text: For dedicated Linux servers (Ubuntu / Debian / RHEL / Docker Engine):

docs.title: Step 1: Clone Repository

git clone https://github.com/RiduanAziz/Robust-Real-Time-Dynamic-Word-Level-American-Sign-Language-Recognition.git signflow
cd signflow

docs.title: Step 2: Bootstrap Assets

Place your models/ directory in the repository root, or run: 

python3 scripts/bootstrap_inference_assets.py --url "<https://github.com/RiduanAziz/Robust-Real-Time-Dynamic-Word-Level-American-Sign-Language-Recognition/releases/tag/v1.0.0-assets>"

# Check readiness (models loaded)

# View live container logs

docs.title: 6. Mobile Testing (iOS & Android)
docs.text:
To test the application from a smartphone:

  1. Deploy the service to an HTTPS provider (such as Render) or use a reverse proxy with a valid SSL certificate.

    Note: Modern mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) require HTTPS to grant camera permissions (navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia).

  2. Open the deployed URL (e.g. https://signflow.onrender.com) on your mobile browser.
  3. When prompted, tap Allow for Camera access.
  4. The frontend will dynamically establish a secure WebSocket stream (wss://.../ws/live).
  5. Ensure good lighting and hold your phone steady or place it on a stand while performing signs.

docs.title: 7. Privacy & Security Safeguards
docs.text:
• Frame Encryption: In production, all video frames sent to /ws/live are encrypted in transit over standard TLS/HTTPS (wss://).
  • Zero Video Retention: Video frames are decoded in memory, processed through MediaPipe and PyTorch inference pipelines, and immediately discarded. Frames are never stored on disk.
  • Connection Limits: The API enforces a concurrency cap (SIGNFLOW_MAX_WS_CONNECTIONS, default: 50) and drops incoming frame payloads larger than 2 MB (MAX_FRAME_BYTES).
  • Non-Root Execution: The production Docker image runs as an unprivileged user (signflow, UID 1000).

docs.title: 8. 100% Free Zero-Cost Deployments (No Credit Card Required)
docs.text:
Cloud platforms like Render, Fly.io, and Railway increasingly require credit card verification even for "free" tiers to prevent abuse. Furthermore, free tiers typically provide only 512 MB RAM, which causes PyTorch and MediaPipe to crash due to Out-Of-Memory (OOMKilled) errors.

For academic defenses, supervisor demos, and examiner reviews, use either of the two 100% free, zero-card methods below:

docs.title: Method 1: Instant Cloudflare Quick Tunnel (Recommended for Demos & Defenses)
docs.text:
Cloudflare provides free, unlimited secure tunnels with no account, no credit card, and no setup.

  • How it works: SignFlow runs locally on your computer with full CPU/GPU and RAM, and Cloudflare exposes an instant public https://*.trycloudflare.com domain with valid SSL encryption.
  • Mobile Camera: Fully functional (mobile browsers require HTTPS to enable camera permissions).
  • WebSocket: Natively supported (wss:// automatic routing).

docs.title: How to Launch:
docs.text:
Double-click share_signflow.bat or run: 

.\start_signflow.ps1 -Public

The script will: 1. Verify inference models and build the frontend bundle. 2. Start the FastAPI backend and verify health. 3. Establish a Cloudflare edge tunnel. 4. Output your Public HTTPS Domain and automatically copy it to your clipboard. 5. You can now send this URL to your supervisor or open it on your phone!

1. Modality Asymmetry:
  2. Body Pose: 99.4% average frame detection rate.

  10. Class Balance:
  11. Training sample count per class ranges from 9 to 25 samples.
  12. Validation and test sets maintain near-uniform per-class support (2 to 4 samples per class).

docs.title: SignFlow: Research Experiment Protocol & Validation Standards
docs.text: Document Version: 2.0.0 (Research Methodology & Tracks A–E) Author: Lead Research & ML Systems Engineer Date: October 2026 Repository: https://github.com/RiduanAziz/Robust-Real-Time-Dynamic-Word-Level-American-Sign-Language-Recognition

docs.title: 1. Experimental Foundations & Non-Negotiable Rules
docs.text:
To ensure scientific validity and reproducibility, all SignFlow experiments must adhere to the following protocol:

  1. Protocol Separation:
  2. Protocol A (Official WLASL Partition): Evaluates against published literature (Li et al. 2020, Pose-TGCN, Uni-Sign). Evaluates 257 held-out test samples. Results disclose documented signer overlap (51 shared signers between train and test).
  3. Protocol B (Signer-Disjoint Partition): Evaluates strict out-of-distribution signer generalization. Zero signer overlap permitted (\(\text{Train Signers} \cap \text{Test Signers} = \emptyset\)).
  4. Canonical Vocabulary Locking:
  5. Vocabulary order and gloss mapping are cryptographically locked via vocabulary_hash: 50a15ecd4abb546fe0e4859713ed6a6c34e4a35caddec1ddc9fdf79c41d19975 (SHA256).
  6. The test set is never re-indexed or filtered to artificially boost accuracy.
  7. Hyperparameter Selection Policy (Zero Test Leakage):
  8. All hyperparameter tuning, model checkpoint selection, early stopping, and ensemble weighting (\(\alpha\)) must be performed strictly using validation set performance.
  9. The final held-out test partition is evaluated exactly once per selected candidate.
  10. Transparent Reporting:
  11. Every evaluation report records: total manifest samples, evaluated samples, excluded samples, Top-1, Top-5, Top-10, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1, and ECE.

• Objective: Independently reproduce the repository's reported baseline using models/robust_holistic_fusion_best.pt on the 257 held-out test samples under Protocol A.

docs.title: Track B — Strong Landmark-Only Architectures
docs.text: Evaluates high-capacity landmark architectures on the verified 1659-dim Holistic representation: 1. Holistic BiGRU (wlasl100_max_accuracy.yaml): 2-layer BiGRU with 128 hidden units, 96-dim embedding, Cosine Annealing warmup, and label smoothing (\(\epsilon=0.08\)). 2. Temporal Convolutional Network (wlasl100_tcn_holistic.yaml): Dilated causal 1D residual convolutions. 3. Temporal Transformer (wlasl100_transformer_colab.yaml): Multi-head self-attention with learned positional embeddings. 4. Reliability-Aware Fusion (wlasl100_reliability_fusion_holistic.yaml): Modality-isolated stream encoders with adaptive reliability gating. 5. Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion (wlasl100_unisign_pgf.yaml): - Multi-scale temporal convolutions + BiGRU kinematics. - Body pose priors guiding hand gesture cross-attention. - Score-aware visibility gating for one-handed signs.

docs.title: Track C — Pretrained Video Models

docs.title: Track D — Probability-Level Ensembling
docs.text:
• Combines complementary candidate architectures: $\(P_{\text{ensemble}}(y | \mathbf{x}) = \alpha P_{\text{baseline}}(y | \mathbf{x}) + (1 - \alpha) P_{\text{candidate}}(y | \mathbf{x})\)$
  • The blending weight \(\alpha \in [0.0, 1.0]\) is tuned strictly on the validation partition to maximize validation Macro-F1.

docs.title: Track E — Empirical Model Selection
docs.text:
• The winning checkpoint is selected based solely on validation Macro-F1 and Top-1 accuracy.
  • Only the selected winner is evaluated on the final held-out test partition.

docs.title: 3.1 Top-1 and Top-K Categorical Accuracy
docs.text:
For \(N\) evaluated test sequences with true class labels \(y_i \in \{0, \dots, C-1\}\) and model logits \(\mathbf{z}_i \in \mathbb{R}^C\):

\[\hat{y}_i^{(1)} = \operatorname{argmax}_{c} z_{i, c}, \quad \text{Top-1} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{1}\left(\hat{y}_i^{(1)} = y_i\right)\] \[\text{Top-K} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{1}\left(y_i \in \operatorname{argtop}_K(\mathbf{z}_i)\right)\]

docs.title: 3.2 Macro-Averaged Precision, Recall, and F1
docs.text: \[\text{Precision}_c = \frac{TP_c}{TP_c + FP_c + \epsilon}, \quad \text{Recall}_c = \frac{TP_c}{TP_c + FN_c + \epsilon}\] \[\text{F1}_c = \frac{2 \cdot \text{Precision}_c \cdot \text{Recall}_c}{\text{Precision}_c + \text{Recall}_c + \epsilon}, \quad \text{Macro-F1} = \frac{1}{C} \sum_{c=0}^{C-1} \text{F1}_c\]

docs.title: 3.3 Expected Calibration Error (ECE)
docs.text:
Partitions predicted probabilities into \(M = 15\) confidence bins \(B_m\):

\[\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} \left| \operatorname{acc}(B_m) - \operatorname{conf}(B_m) \right|\]

docs.title: Feature Engineering Audit and Results — SignFlow WLASL-100
docs.text: Document Version: 2.0.0 (Feature Contracts & Spatial Representations) Author: Lead Research & ML Systems Engineer Date: October 2026 Artifact Dependencies: - src/sign_language/features/representations.py - src/sign_language/landmarks/schema.py - tests/test_features_contract.py

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Defect Resolutions
docs.text: This document provides the authoritative engineering specification and verification results for all landmark feature representations in SignFlow.

docs.title: 1.1 Resolution of Dimensionality Discrepancies
docs.text:
• Previous Contradiction: _FEATURES["engineered"] declared feature_dim = 280 in representations.py, but the actual implementation concatenated: $\(\text{Hands+Pose (225)} + \text{Left Wrist-Rel (63)} + \text{Right Wrist-Rel (63)} + \text{Inter-Wrist (4)} + \text{Fingertip Extensions (10)} = 365\)$ This 85-dimension contradiction caused silent padding/slicing errors in downstream models expecting 280 features.
  • Resolution:
  • The specification has been officially updated to feature_dim = 365.
  • Strict mask propagation has been implemented for all derived features.
  • Zero-filling is enforced when any required keypoint is missing.
  • An automated regression test suite (tests/test_features_contract.py) validates that declared dimensions and actual outputs match 100%.

docs.title: 2. Supported Feature Representations (Representations A–F)
docs.text: Rep ID Representation Name Feature Dim Input Modalities Description & Formulation A hands 126 Left Hand (63), Right Hand (63) 21 3D coordinates per hand (\(21 \times 3 \times 2 = 126\)). B hands_pose 225 Hands (126), Body Pose (99) Hands plus 33 body pose landmarks (\(33 \times 3 = 99\)). C holistic 1,659 Hands (126), Pose (99), Face (1434) Full MediaPipe holistic mesh (553 3D keypoints). Essential for face-anchored signs. D engineered 365 Hands (126), Pose (99) + Spatial Relations Hands+Pose (225) + Wrist-rel (126) + Inter-wrist distance (4) + Fingertip extensions (10). E holistic_dynamics 4,977 Full Holistic + Velocity + Acceleration Positions (\(1659\)) + First-order differences (\(1659\)) + Second-order differences (\(1659\)). F anatomical_streams Multi-stream Isolated LH, RH, Pose, Face Stream-isolated tensor inputs for Prior-Guided Fusion (UniSignPGFClassifier).

docs.title: 3. Strict Validity Mask Propagation
docs.text:
Derived kinematic and spatial features must propagate missing landmark masks rather than falsely reporting valid data for zero-filled values:

  1. Wrist-Relative Coordinates (63 dims per hand): $\(\mathbf{p}_{i}^{\text{rel}} = \mathbf{p}_{i} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{wrist}}, \quad m_{i}^{\text{rel}} = m_{i} \times m_{\text{wrist}}\)$ Rule: If the wrist is undetected, all wrist-relative coordinates for that hand are masked out (\(m = 0.0\)) and zero-filled.
  2. Inter-Wrist Displacement & Distance (4 dims): $\(\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{p}_{\text{rh\_wrist}} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{lh\_wrist}}, \quad d_{\text{norm}} = \|\mathbf{d}\|_2, \quad m_{\text{inter}} = m_{\text{lh\_wrist}} \times m_{\text{rh\_wrist}}\)$ Rule: Both wrists must be visible for inter-hand interaction features to be considered valid.
  3. Fingertip Extension Distances (10 dims): $\(e_k = \|\mathbf{p}_{\text{tip}_k} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{wrist}}\|_2, \quad m_{e_k} = m_{\text{tip}_k} \times m_{\text{wrist}}\)$ Rule: Extension distance is only valid if both the fingertip (indices 4, 8, 12, 16, 20) and the wrist are detected.

docs.title: 4. Geometry-Aware Spatial Normalization
docs.text: SignFlow rejects naive flat-vector mean-centering. Instead, spatial normalization is computed per-frame based on anatomically meaningful reference frames: - Torso / Shoulder Frame: Shoulders (pose landmarks 11, 12) establish the horizontal scale and body center. - Local Hand Coordinates: Each hand's internal geometry is preserved relative to its wrist coordinate. - Face Mesh Independence: The 478 face landmarks are centered on the nose bridge / eye midpoint so their high point count does not dominate the global coordinate center of the signing space.

docs.title: SignFlow: Robust Real-Time Dynamic Word-Level American Sign Language Recognition
Comprehensive Internship Final Project Report
docs.text: Project Title: Robust Real-Time Dynamic Word-Level American Sign Language Recognition Using Landmark Kinematics, Prior-Guided Fusion, and Calibrated Probability Ensembles Student / Intern Name: Riduan Aziz Organization / Department: Machine Learning & Computer Vision Research Team Supervisors / Mentors: Senior ML Systems Architect & Computer Vision Lead Academic / Internship Period: 2026 Repository: GitHub: RiduanAziz/Robust-Real-Time-Dynamic-Word-Level-American-Sign-Language-Recognition Primary Benchmark: World-Level American Sign Language 100-Class Benchmark (WLASL-100)

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Word-level American Sign Language (ASL) recognition in uncontrolled real-world environments presents profound computer vision challenges, including fast non-rigid hand articulation, high interpersonal signer variability, severe modality asymmetry, and extreme class overlap. Existing RGB video-based approaches (such as 3D Convolutional Neural Networks) impose excessive computational burdens (~500 ms/sample) that prohibit deployment on edge devices, while raw coordinate-based graph networks frequently degrade under missing or occluded hand detections.

This project delivers SignFlow, an end-to-end, high-performance, and verifiable machine learning system for real-time word-level ASL recognition. Through systematic exploratory data analysis of 2,038 WLASL-100 sequences and 21,083 nationwide landmark archives, we uncover critical real-world phenomena: pose and face landmarks exhibit high stability (>97% visibility), whereas non-dominant hands are absent in up to 67.5% of signing frames. To overcome these challenges, we designed and implemented: 1. A 553-keypoint Holistic Landmark Normalization & Feature Pipeline (1,659 coordinates spanning body pose, face mesh, and bilateral hands) backed by mathematically sound visibility masking. 2. An adapted Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion (PGF) architecture that leverages body/face anatomical priors to guide hand attention alongside score-aware reliability gating. 3. A 3-Way Probability-Level Calibrated Ensemble combining baseline temporal BiGRUs, deep regularized BiGRUs, and cross-attentive PGF models.

Tuned strictly on the validation partition (\(N=337\)) via a 3-simplex grid search with zero test-set leakage, our ensemble achieves a new defensible benchmark on the official WLASL-100 held-out test split (\(N=257\)): 76.65% Top-1 Accuracy (+2.33% over baseline), 91.44% Top-5 Accuracy (+2.72% over baseline), 94.16% Top-10 Accuracy, a Macro-F1 of 0.7558, and cuts the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by 47.6% down to 0.0838. We successfully deployed this pipeline into a production-grade, full-stack assistive workstation featuring an asynchronous FastAPI WebSocket engine, a modern React/TypeScript glassmorphism frontend, dynamic model switching, and real-time multi-camera streaming operating at ~31.7 ms inference latency (~42.5 FPS).

docs.title: 1.1 Context and Significance
docs.text: Over 70 million deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals worldwide rely on sign languages as their primary medium of communication. Despite advances in automatic speech recognition (ASR) for spoken languages, dynamic sign language recognition (SLR) remains drastically underserved. Sign language is not a simple sequence of static finger gestures; it is an expressive, multidimensional language consisting of: - Manual Features: Dynamic trajectory of the hands, finger shape conformations, and palm orientations. - Non-Manual Markers: Facial expressions, lip patterns, eye gaze, and head movements that act as critical grammatical markers. - Spatial Anchors: Body torso and shoulder alignments that provide the spatial context against which signs are articulated.

docs.title: 1.2 Core Engineering and Scientific Challenges
docs.text: Developing an interactive, real-time, word-level ASL recognition system faces five fundamental roadblocks: 1. Modality Occlusion and Asymmetry: Signers frequently perform one-handed signs or cross hands over the body, causing camera self-occlusion. In standard models, missing keypoints default to zero coordinates, creating artificial high-velocity motion vectors that corrupt temporal representations. 2. Computational Constraints in Assistive Tech: Deploying heavy 3D-CNNs (e.g., I3D, SlowFast) directly on client laptops or web browsers introduces unviable latency (>400 ms), high power consumption, and frame lag. 3. Severe Signer Contamination in Published Research: Standard public splits often mix the same signer across training and test partitions, resulting in inflated academic metrics that collapse when exposed to novel signers in real-world environments. 4. Model Overconfidence & Calibration: Softmax probabilities in standard neural networks often exhibit high calibration error, producing misleading certainty on erroneous predictions. 5. Training-Serving Skew: Discrepancies between preprocessed offline datasets and real-time streaming camera frames degrade runtime accuracy.

docs.title: 1.3 Project Objectives
docs.text: The overarching objectives of this internship project were to: - Establish a reproducible, deterministic ML training and evaluation pipeline on the WLASL-100 benchmark. - Conduct deep exploratory data audits to identify dataset leakage, class imbalance, and landmark detection characteristics. - Implement novel deep learning architectures incorporating anatomical prior guidance and reliability gating. - Build a zero-leakage probability ensemble achieving superior accuracy and calibration over historical baselines. - Develop a full-stack, real-time web application with sub-40 ms latency, dynamic model selection, and multi-camera support.

docs.title: 2.1 Video-Based vs. Landmark-Based Recognition
docs.text:
Prior research in sign language recognition broadly falls into two categories:

Approach Typical Architectures Pros Cons RGB Video-Based 3D-CNNs (I3D, SlowFast), Video Transformers (TimeSformer) Captures subtle texture, lighting, and ambient context. High parameter counts (>25M), severe compute costs (~500 ms/sample), privacy risks. Skeletal / Landmark-Based Spatial-Temporal Graph Networks (ST-GCN), BiGRUs, Spatial Transformers Lightweight, privacy-preserving, fast inference (<35 ms), focus purely on kinematics. Sensitive to joint estimation noise, requires robust normalization.

In this project, we adopted a holistic landmark-based approach, leveraging MediaPipe's high-efficiency keypoint extractors to achieve low latency while extracting geometric representations from 553 holistic keypoints.

docs.title: 4.1 Holistic Landmark Normalization & Feature Engineering
docs.text: SignFlow processes raw MediaPipe landmarks through a multistage geometric normalization pipeline: 1. Torso Centering: Coordinates are translated such that the midpoint between the left and right shoulders resides at the origin \((0, 0, 0)\). 2. Scale Invariance: Distances are normalized by the Euclidean distance between the left and right shoulders (\(d_{\text{shoulder}}\)). 3. Engineered Kinematic Representation (365 Dimensions): - Base Hands + Pose: \(21 \times 3 \times 2 + 33 \times 3 = 225\) dimensions. - Wrist-Relative Hand Coordinates: \(21 \times 3 = 63\) dimensions per hand (\(126\) total). - Inter-Wrist Vector & Distance: \(3 + 1 = 4\) dimensions. - Fingertip Extensions: Euclidean distances from fingertips (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky) to the respective wrist (\(5 \times 2 = 10\) dimensions). - Strict Masking Contract: Derived features are masked to zero unless both participating landmarks have non-zero visibility flags, preventing ghost artifacts.

docs.title: 1. Baseline BiGRU (robust_holistic_fusion)
docs.text:
• Architecture: 2-layer Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (hidden dimension 128, dropout 0.3).
  • Input: Flattened 1,659-dim holistic coordinates.
  • Temporal pooling: Attentive temporal pooling aggregating hidden states across the sequence.

docs.title: 2. Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion Classifier (UniSignPGFClassifier)
docs.text: Adapted from the ICLR 2025 research (Uni-Sign: Prior-Guided Fusion for Dynamic Sign Language Recognition, arXiv:2501.15187): - Isolated Anatomical Encoders: Four separate 1D convolutional residual blocks project Left Hand, Right Hand, Body Pose, and Face Mesh independently into latent dimension \(d=64\). - Prior-Guided Cross-Attention: Body pose and face mesh act as spatial Keys and Values, while hand feature representations act as Queries. This explicitly answers: "Where are the hands moving relative to the face and shoulders?" - Score-Aware Reliability Gating: Computes an empirical reliability score \(r_m = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{1}(\|\mathbf{x}_{m, t}\| > 0)\) for each hand. The attention outputs are scaled by \(r_m\), gracefully suppressing noise when a hand is absent. - Classification Head: Kinematic BiGRU temporal aggregation followed by layer normalization and linear projection.

docs.title: 3. Deep BiGRU with Maximum Regularization (wlasl100_max_accuracy)
docs.text:
• Deeper hidden capacity (embedding dimension 96, hidden dimension 128).
  • Trained with Label Smoothing (\(\epsilon = 0.08\)) and a Cosine Annealing Learning Rate Scheduler over 200 epochs to prevent overconfidence.

docs.title: 5.1 Ensembling Theory & Objective
docs.text: Rather than relying on a single model's inductive bias, we combine the complementary strengths of our three distinct paradigms: $\(\mathbf{P}_{\text{ensemble}} = w_1 \mathbf{P}_{\text{Baseline}} + w_2 \mathbf{P}_{\text{UniSign}} + w_3 \mathbf{P}_{\text{DeepBiGRU}}, \quad \text{where } \sum_{i=1}^3 w_i = 1, \; w_i \ge 0\)$

docs.title: 5.2 Mathematical Formulation of Metrics
docs.text:
• Top-\(k\) Accuracy: $\(\text{Top-}k = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{1}(y_i \in \text{top\_k\_indices}(\mathbf{p}_i))\)$
  • Expected Calibration Error (ECE): $\(\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} \left| \text{acc}(B_m) - \text{conf}(B_m) \right|\)$ where predictions are grouped into \(M=10\) confidence bins \(B_m\).

docs.title: 5.3 Zero-Leakage Validation Grid Search
docs.text: To ensure rigorous scientific integrity, optimal weights \((w_1, w_2, w_3)\) were discovered through an exhaustive 3-simplex grid search evaluated strictly on the 337 validation samples (validation_manifest.json): - Search Space: \(w_i \in [0.0, 1.0]\) with step size \(\Delta = 0.05\), constrained to \(w_1 + w_2 + w_3 = 1.0\). - Validation Result: Optimal configuration \((w_1=0.25, w_2=0.10, w_3=0.65)\) achieved 78.34% Validation Top-1 (264 / 337 correct). - The weights were then locked and applied in a single forward pass to the 257 held-out test samples.

  • Live Recognition Dashboard: Displays top-5 confidence bars, ECE calibration indicators, token prediction history, and text-to-speech audio synthesis via the Web Speech API.

docs.title: 8.1 Uncovering Signer Contamination in Published Research
docs.text: During our dataset audit, we uncovered a significant methodological flaw in standard WLASL benchmarks: - Protocol A (Official Benchmark Partition): 104 out of 105 test signers (99.0%) appear in the training split. Models evaluated under Protocol A benefit from recognizing the physical body proportions of known individuals. - Protocol B (Signer-Independent Partition): We constructed data/manifests/signer_disjoint/, enforcing zero signer overlap. When evaluating on completely unseen signers, accuracy naturally declines, highlighting the true out-of-distribution challenge of dynamic sign recognition.

docs.title: 8.2 Discovered Implementation Discrepancies and Repairs
docs.text: During the internship pipeline audit, we discovered and resolved three critical discrepancies: 1. Engineered Feature Dimension Mismatch: The feature dimension was declared as 280, but the concatenation code generated 365 features. We updated the contract, added visibility propagation, and locked it with automated regression tests (test_features_contract.py). 2. Vocabulary Index Alignment: Configuration files had disparate label orderings, causing an apparent drop to 9.30% when evaluating with unaligned YAML files. We established a canonical hash-locked vocabulary across all configurations. 3. Modality Visibility Dropout: Missing hands caused arbitrary zero-velocity jumps. Resolved via the score-aware gating mechanism in Uni-Sign PGF.

docs.title: 9.1 Summary of Contributions
docs.text: Through this internship project, we: 1. Successfully reproduced and validated the WLASL-100 baseline at 74.32% Top-1 accuracy. 2. Designed and adapted an ICLR 2025 Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion network achieving state-of-the-art calibration (ECE 0.0561). 3. Created a zero-leakage 3-Way Probability Ensemble achieving 76.65% Top-1 and 91.44% Top-5 accuracy on the official held-out test benchmark. 4. Delivered a fully functional, production-grade real-time web application with dynamic model and camera switching operating at 31.7 ms glass-to-glass latency. 5. Backed every component with 19 automated regression tests and comprehensive documentation.

docs.title: 9.2 Future Research Roadmap
docs.text:
• Continuous Sign Language Recognition (CSLR): Expanding from isolated word recognition to continuous sentence translation using Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and causal language modeling.
  • On-Device Edge Acceleration: Compiling the ensemble weights to ONNX Runtime / WebAssembly for complete client-side, serverless browser execution.
  • Multi-Signer Few-Shot Adaptation: Implementing test-time normalization to adapt to unseen signers in fewer than 3 calibration frames.

docs.title: SignFlow: Landmark Quality & Extraction Diagnostic Report
docs.text: Audit Date: October 26, 2026 Extractor Asset: models/mediapipe/holistic_landmarker.task MediaPipe Version: MediaPipe 1.0.1

docs.title: 1. Landmark Schema & Coordinate Conventions
docs.text:
SignFlow processes human upper-body kinematics via Google MediaPipe Holistic Landmarker:

Kinematic Stream Joint Count Coordinates per Joint Flattened Dims Coordinate Conventions Left Hand 21 keypoints \((x, y, z)\) 63 Normalized \([0, 1]\) image space; \(z\) represents relative depth. Right Hand 21 keypoints \((x, y, z)\) 63 Normalized \([0, 1]\) image space; \(z\) represents relative depth. Pose (Upper Body) 33 keypoints \((x, y, z)\) 99 Body joints including shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips. Face Mesh 478 keypoints \((x, y, z)\) 1,434 Detailed facial contours and lip articulation. Total Holistic 553 keypoints \((x, y, z)\) 1,659 Full multi-stream holistic observation per frame.

docs.title: 2. Missing-Data & Occlusion Handling Strategy
docs.text:
In real-world signing, one-handed signs or rapid out-of-frame gestures cause temporary tracking dropouts. Interpreting an absent hand as coordinates at the origin \((0, 0, 0)\) introduces severe artificial motion vectors that deceive temporal neural networks.

SignFlow enforces an explicit missing-data contract (src/sign_language/landmarks/missing_data.py):

  1. Explicit Validity Masks: Every frame maintains a boolean vector \(\mathbf{m}_t \in \{0, 1\}^D\) distinguishing actively observed keypoints from missing keypoints.
  2. Conservative Short-Gap Interpolation:
  3. For temporary dropouts of length \(\Delta t \le 3\) frames (e.g. rapid motion blur), linear interpolation reconstructs the trajectory between confident keyframes: $\(\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{x}_{t_{\text{prev}}} + \frac{t - t_{\text{prev}}}{t_{\text{next}} - t_{\text{prev}}} \left(\mathbf{x}_{t_{\text{next}}} - \mathbf{x}_{t_{\text{prev}}}\right)\)$
  4. Gaps longer than 3 frames are never hallucinated. Long gaps remain marked as invalid, and the proposed Reliability-Aware fusion layer (M6) dynamically downweights the absent modality.
  5. Dynamics Calculation Protection: Velocities and accelerations are never computed across missing or discontinuous frames, preventing spurious extreme acceleration spikes.

docs.title: 3. Evaluated Input Representations
docs.text:
SignFlow supports four distinct geometric and kinematic representations:

  • Representation A (Hands Only, \(D = 126\)):
  • Left hand (\(21 \times 3\)) and right hand (\(21 \times 3\)). Minimal computation, but loses arm posture and shoulder orientation.
  • Representation B (Hands + Body Pose, \(D = 225\)):
  • Hands (\(42 \times 3\)) plus 33 body pose keypoints. Captures arm angle and torso anchoring without facial mesh overhead.
  • Representation C (Holistic Full, \(D = 1,659\) static / \(4,977\) dynamic):
  • Hands, pose, and face, with optional first-order velocity (\(\Delta \mathbf{x}\)) and second-order acceleration (\(\Delta^2 \mathbf{x}\)).
  • Representation D (Engineered Features, \(D = 257\)):
  • Implemented in src/sign_language/features/representations.py.
  • Computes wrist-relative joint coordinates (scale and translation invariant).
  • Computes 3D Euclidean inter-wrist distance (measuring two-hand proximity).
  • Computes finger flexion and extension angles across MCP, PIP, and DIP joints.

docs.title: 4. Extraction Failure & Latency Profile
docs.text: Empirical benchmarking (results/realtime_benchmark.json) reveals: - Mean Extraction Latency on CPU: ~0.7 to 1.5 ms per frame once initialized (\(480\times360\)). - Cold-Start Overhead: First-frame MediaPipe kernel initialization requires ~500–2,000 ms on CPU. Subsequent frames stream steadily at 25–32 FPS. - Dimension Caching Edge Case: MediaPipe's SegmentationSmoothingCalculator caches image dimensions. Switching resolutions dynamically requires extractor re-instantiation to prevent dimension check assertions.

docs.text: This guide details how to integrate and serve trained SignFlow models (including the reproduced baseline and newly trained Uni-Sign PGF / high-accuracy models) into the local FastAPI backend and real-time React/TypeScript frontend.

docs.text:

├── config.yaml                 # Complete model architecture & training configuration

docs.text:
The FastAPI server is implemented in src/sign_language/api/app.py. Configure the active model checkpoint in configs/base.yaml or via environment variables:

# Set environment variables (optional overrides)
export SIGNFLOW_MODEL_PATH="models/robust_holistic_fusion_best.pt"

python -m uvicorn sign_language.api.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

docs.text:

  • POST /predict/sequence: Offline batch sequence classification (accepts [T, 1659] landmark array).
  • WS /ws/stream: Real-time WebSocket connection for streaming MediaPipe landmark frames.

docs.title: 4. Real-Time Dynamic Sequence Processing
docs.text:
Dynamic ASL gestures unfold over time (\(1.0\) to \(3.5\) seconds). The streaming inference engine adheres to the following real-time rules:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Camera as Webcam / Frontend
    participant MediaPipe as MediaPipe Tasks (JS/Wasm)
    participant Engine as SignFlow Sequence Buffer
    participant Model as PyTorch Classifier Head

    Camera->>MediaPipe: Video Frame (30 FPS)
    MediaPipe->>Engine: Stream 553 Holistic Keypoints (1659 coords) + Mask
    Note over Engine: Sliding Window Buffer (Size: 64 frames)
    alt Buffer < 16 frames
        Engine-->>Camera: Status: "Buffering / Insufficient Sequence"
    else Buffer >= 16 frames
        Engine->>Engine: Temporal Interpolation to T=64
        Engine->>Engine: Anatomical Normalization & Mask Propagation
        Engine->>Model: Forward Pass [1, 64, 1659]
        Model-->>Engine: Logits & Softmax Probabilities
        alt Confidence > Threshold & Not Duplicated
            Engine-->>Camera: Emit Recognized Sign Gloss
        else Low Confidence / Identical Sign
            Engine-->>Camera: Suppress Emission
        end
    end

docs.title: 4.1 Temporal Commitment Logic
docs.text: To prevent rapid repeated emissions of the same sign: 1. Confidence Threshold: Minimum softmax probability (default \(\tau = 0.65\)). 2. Debounce Interval: Minimum cooldown of \(1.2\) seconds before re-emitting the same gloss. 3. Rest-Position Detection: Hand return to resting position below chest automatically flushes the sliding buffer.

docs.title: 5. Latency & Resource Benchmarks
docs.text: Measured on standard host CPU: - MediaPipe Landmark Extraction: \(\approx 18.5\text{ ms}\) per frame. - Preprocessing & Resampling: \(\approx 0.8\text{ ms}\) per sequence. - Model Inference (robust_holistic_fusion): \(\approx 4.2\text{ ms}\) on CPU (\(0.9\text{ ms}\) on CUDA). - Model Inference (unisign_pgf): \(\approx 8.1\text{ ms}\) on CPU (\(1.4\text{ ms}\) on CUDA). - Total Pipeline Latency: \(< 35\text{ ms}\), ensuring real-time 30 FPS interactive capability.

docs.title: 3.1 Feature Engineering Schema Parity
docs.text:
• Finding: In src/sign_language/features/representations.py, _FEATURES["engineered"] had feature_dim = 280, but the concatenation function produced 365 dimensions: $\(\text{Base Hands+Pose (225)} + \text{Left Wrist-Rel (63)} + \text{Right Wrist-Rel (63)} + \text{Inter-Hand (4)} + \text{Fingertip Extensions (10)} = 365\)$
  • Fix: Updated _FEATURES["engineered"].feature_dim = 365. Implemented strict mask propagation:
  • Wrist-relative coordinates are only valid if both the landmark and the wrist are visible.
  • Inter-wrist distance is only valid if both wrists are visible.
  • Fingertip extension distances are only valid if both the fingertip and the wrist are visible.
  • Verification: New unit test tests/test_features_contract.py validates dimension, masking, and boundary conditions.

docs.title: 3.2 Canonical Vocabulary Alignment
docs.text:
• Finding: configs/colab/wlasl100_max_accuracy.yaml, configs/base.yaml, and configs/dataset.yaml contained differing class orders and label subsets. Evaluating the baseline model against configs/base.yaml previously yielded 9.30% because of label index permutations.
  • Fix: Programmatically aligned all configuration files to the canonical baseline vocabulary (hash: 50a15ecd4abb546fe0e4859713ed6a6c34e4a35caddec1ddc9fdf79c41d19975).
  • Result: configs/base.yaml now reproduces the exact 74.32% Top-1 and 88.72% Top-5 baseline.

docs.title: 3.3 Uni-Sign Architecture Integration
docs.text:
• Finding: Uni-Sign (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2501.15187) achieves 92.25% on WLASL-100 by utilizing Prior-Guided Fusion (PGF). In this paradigm, skeletal body pose acts as a spatial reference anchor for hand gestures, and score-aware reliability gating prevents noise from missing or occluded hands.
  • Fix: Created src/sign_language/models/unisign_pgf.py (UniSignPGFClassifier), featuring:
  • 4 isolated anatomical encoders (Left Hand, Right Hand, Body Pose, Face Mesh).
  • Multi-scale 1D temporal convolutions (kernel sizes 3 and 5) with residual connections.
  • Prior-Guided Cross-Attention where hand queries attend to body/face anchors.
  • Score-aware reliability gating for one-handed signs.
  • Bidirectional kinematic recurrent layers and calibrated classification head.
  • Verification: Registered in src/sign_language/models/factory.py and forward-pass verified on both 1659-dim Holistic and 225-dim Hands+Pose inputs.

docs.title: SignFlow Model Card: Robust Holistic Fusion Classifier
1. Model Details
docs.text:
• Model Name: SignFlow Robust Holistic Fusion Classifier (RobustHolisticFusionClassifier)
  • Version: 2.0-research
  • Model Type: Deep Spatiotemporal Neural Network with Multi-Stream Gated Modality Fusion
  • Developers: SignFlow Research Team
  • Framework: PyTorch 2.0+
  • License: MIT License
  • Target Vocabulary: WLASL-100 (100 American Sign Language isolated dynamic words)

docs.title: 2. Intended Use
docs.text:
• Primary Use: Real-time assistive word-level American Sign Language recognition from webcam video streams or prerecorded signing clips.
  • Intended Users: Deaf, hard-of-hearing, and hearing individuals communicating via ASL; accessibility researchers; educational applications.
  • Out-of-Scope Uses:
  • Continuous sentence-level sign language translation without isolated word segmentation.
  • Non-ASL sign languages (e.g., British Sign Language, Bengali Sign Language, Auslan) without retraining.
  • Critical life-safety or emergency translation without human verification.

docs.title: 3. Input & Output Contract
docs.text:
• Input Tensors:
  • landmarks: Float32 tensor of shape (Batch, SequenceLength=64, InputDim=1659) representing normalized 3D upper-body landmarks (Left Hand: 63, Right Hand: 63, Pose: 99, Face Mesh: 1434).
  • mask: Float32 boolean tensor of shape (Batch, SequenceLength=64) indicating active vs padded frames.
  • Output Tensors:
  • logits: Float32 tensor of shape (Batch, NumClasses=100).
  • Top-1 and Top-5 class predictions with associated softmax probabilities.

docs.title: 4. Performance & Benchmark Summary
docs.text:
• Protocol A (Official WLASL Benchmark, 257 held-out test samples):
  • Top-1 Accuracy: 74.32%
  • Top-5 Accuracy: 88.72%
  • Top-10 Accuracy: 94.16%
  • Macro-F1 Score: 0.7213
  • Weighted-F1 Score: 0.7257

docs.title: 5. Ethical Considerations & Bias
docs.text:
• Signer Diversity: Protocol A training data exhibits signer overlap with the test set. Models deployed in production may experience accuracy degradation on signers with different skin tones, hand proportions, or signing cadences.

docs.title: 1. The 2-Minute Executive Pitch (Opening Statement)
docs.text:
"Distinguished committee and mentors, dynamic word-level sign language recognition represents one of the most demanding frontiers in human-computer interaction. While state-of-the-art vision models typically rely on heavy 3D-CNNs that take 500 milliseconds per sample and cannot run in real time on edge hardware, standard landmark models break down when signers occlude their hands or perform one-handed gestures.

In this internship, I developed SignFlow—an end-to-end, high-performance recognition ecosystem. My work delivers three key breakthroughs: 1. First, I audited the 2,038-sequence WLASL-100 benchmark and uncovered critical real-world modality asymmetries: non-dominant hands are absent in two-thirds of signing frames, proving that naive zero-imputation creates artificial high-velocity motion noise. 2. Second, to solve this, I designed and adapted an ICLR 2025 Uni-Sign Prior-Guided Fusion network with score-aware reliability gating, and combined it with regularized deep recurrent models into a 3-Way Probability Ensemble. Tuned strictly on validation data with zero test leakage, our ensemble sets a new benchmark: 76.65% Top-1 Accuracy (+2.33% over baseline), 91.44% Top-5 Accuracy, and reduces calibration error by 47.6%. 3. Third, rather than stopping at an offline notebook, I built and verified a full-stack production workstation using FastAPI WebSockets and a React 18 glassmorphic frontend that supports live multi-camera input and dynamic model switching with an end-to-end latency of just 31.7 milliseconds.

Every result in this project is reproducible via deterministic scripts and backed by 19 automated regression tests. I am excited to walk you through the architecture, the empirical discoveries, and a live demonstration."

docs.title: Q1: "Why did you use MediaPipe holistic landmarks instead of an end-to-end video model like I3D or SlowFast?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Testing your understanding of the latency-accuracy-privacy trade-off in assistive technology.
  • Your Answer:

    "End-to-end 3D-CNNs like I3D achieve ~65.89% Top-1 on WLASL-100 (Li et al., 2020), but require approximately 500 milliseconds per sample on a desktop GPU and tens of gigabytes of VRAM. In an assistive system, deaf users require immediate real-time feedback (<50 ms glass-to-glass latency). Furthermore, raw RGB video introduces substantial user privacy concerns in domestic or workplace settings. By decoupling perception via client-side MediaPipe extraction, we stream 553 geometric coordinates instead of high-bandwidth video, preserving privacy and shrinking end-to-end inference latency to ~31.7 milliseconds (over 15x faster than I3D) while achieving a superior 76.65% Top-1 accuracy."

docs.title: Q2: "How did you ensure there was zero data leakage when finding the ensemble weights?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Checking scientific integrity and hyperparameter overfitting.
  • Your Answer:

    "We strictly followed an isolated partition protocol. The ensemble weights \((w_1, w_2, w_3)\) were optimized via an exhaustive 3-simplex grid search exclusively on the 337 validation samples (data/manifests/validation_manifest.json). The optimal configuration—\((0.25, 0.10, 0.65)\)—was selected based solely on validation Top-1 accuracy (78.34%). Only after these weights were completely locked was the ensemble evaluated in a single forward pass on the 257 held-out test samples. The test set was never accessed during hyperparameter tuning, preventing any data snooping or leakage."

docs.title: Q3: "Solo Uni-Sign achieved 70.43% Top-1, which is lower than the 74.32% baseline. Why include it in the ensemble?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Testing whether you understand ensemble theory and complementary inductive biases.
  • Your Answer:

    "In ensembling, the goal is not to combine models with identical error profiles, but to combine models with orthogonal inductive biases. While the baseline BiGRU models temporal sequential transitions, Uni-Sign PGF explicitly models spatial cross-attention between hands and body anchors. Most importantly, Uni-Sign possesses exceptional probability calibration: its Expected Calibration Error (ECE) is 0.0561, compared to 0.1598 for the baseline. When blended with the baseline and deep BiGRU, Uni-Sign dampens overconfident incorrect predictions. This complementary spatial-temporal bias is why the ensemble jumped to 76.65% Top-1 and reduced overall ECE by 47.6%."

docs.title: Q4: "What is the significance of your EDA findings on hand detection rates?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Verifying whether you actually analyzed the dataset before training models.
  • Your Answer:

    "Our empirical audit across the 2,038 sequences revealed that body pose (99.4%) and face mesh (97.3%) are almost universally visible, but the right hand is present in only 63.6% of frames, and the left hand in only 32.5%. In sign language, many signs are unilateral (one-handed). Naive concatenation imputes missing hands with \((0, 0, 0)\), creating artificial high-velocity motion vectors when hands appear or disappear. This discovery directly inspired our reliability gating mechanism, where hand attention maps are scaled by their empirical presence score \(r_m\), mathematically zeroing out artificial gradient noise."

docs.title: Q5: "What is the difference between Protocol A and Protocol B, and why does it matter?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Testing your awareness of academic benchmark flaws and real-world generalization.
  • Your Answer:

    "Protocol A is the official WLASL benchmark split. However, our audit revealed that 104 out of 105 signers (99.0%) in the test set also appear in the training set. While this allows models to learn signer-specific biometric habits, it does not evaluate how the model handles unseen people. To address this, we engineered Protocol B (data/manifests/signer_disjoint/), which strictly partitions signers with zero overlap. Protocol A proves that our architecture outperforms published literature under standard conditions (76.65% vs 74.32%), while Protocol B provides an honest, rigorous foundation for evaluating true out-of-distribution generalizability."

docs.title: Q6: "How does the system perform when deployed to a real webcam in a web browser?"
docs.text:
• Examiner's Intent: Assessing full-stack deployment, systems architecture, and practical engineering.
  • Your Answer:

    "We built an end-to-end full-stack application. In the frontend (React 18 / TypeScript), MediaPipe's WebAssembly pipeline processes camera frames client-side and transmits normalized landmarks over a persistent WebSocket connection to an asynchronous FastAPI backend. The backend maintains a rolling FIFO window of 64 frames. Complete round-trip processing takes ~31.7 ms, allowing us to run at 30+ frames per second. Furthermore, our frontend includes a dynamic camera selector allowing users to switch video inputs on the fly, and a model selector that hot-switches inference architectures without server restarts."

docs.title: 2. Key Engineering Findings
docs.text:
1. Sweet Spot Recommendation:
  2. \(480\times360\) at JPEG Quality 75 is the optimal operating point. It yields ~13.5 KB payload per frame, ~31.7 ms median end-to-end latency, and sustained ~31.6 FPS on host CPU.
  3. Network Bandwidth Consumption:
  4. Streaming \(480\times360\) at Quality 75 at 25 FPS consumes only ~338 KB/sec (~2.7 Mbps), well within standard residential broadband and mobile 4G/5G connections.
  5. Pipeline Bottleneck Attribution:
  6. Network encode/decode: ~1.5–2.5 ms (negligible).
  7. Landmark extraction: ~0.7–1.5 ms on CPU once warmed up.
  8. Model inference: ~28–32 ms on CPU. (Projected to drop to < 5 ms on GPU via TensorRT or CUDA).
  9. Webcam Real-World Disclosure:
  10. The measurements above were obtained using prerecorded MP4 frames passed through the full pipeline. Physical user webcam performance remains dependent on local lighting, camera sensor frame rates (e.g. 30Hz limit), and browser execution.

docs.title: Reference Repository Review
docs.text: This document records the architectural, algorithmic, licensing, and implementation findings from inspecting reference repositories and standards for Robust Real-Time Dynamic Word-Level American Sign Language Recognition.

docs.title: Reference A: Official WLASL
docs.text:
• Repository URL: https://github.com/dxli94/WLASL
  • Inspected Files:
  • code/TGCN/data_reader.py: Data ingestion, gloss-to-instance mapping, missing video handling.
  • code/I3D/train_i3d.py & code/I3D/pytorch_i3d.py: 3D CNN RGB video baseline.
  • code/TGCN/models.py: Pose-TGCN (Temporal Graph Convolutional Network on 2D OpenPose keypoints).
  • data/WLASL_v0.3.json: Primary dataset metadata (glosses, instances, bounding boxes, URLs, signers, splits).
  • data/nslt_100.json, nslt_300.json, nslt_1000.json, nslt_2000.json: Official split indices.
  • C-UDA-1.0.pdf: Computational Use of Data Agreement.
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Direct task match: WLASL is the benchmark dataset used in this thesis.
  • Relevant for dataset schema, gloss index conventions, split evaluation protocol (Top-1, Top-5, Top-10), and handling broken/unavailable YouTube links.
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • WLASL uses OpenPose 2D landmarks (body pose + hands, 27 joints total for Pose-TGCN) or dense RGB video frames for I3D.
  • Evaluates across subsets: WLASL-100, WLASL-300, WLASL-1000, WLASL-2000.
  • Evaluates standard train/val/test splits, though the original splits contain signer overlap across partitions.
  • License & Restrictions:
  • C-UDA-1.0 (Computational Use of Data Agreement).
  • Raw videos and extracted features must remain local and cannot be redistributed. Third-party checkpoints must not be distributed without authorization.
  • Dataset citation required: Li et al., "Word-level Deep Sign Language Recognition from Video: A New Large-scale Dataset and Methods Comparison", WACV 2020.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Deterministic gloss-to-ID mapping derived from sorted glosses.
  • Exact sample matching using video_id.
  • Machine-readable tracking of missing/unreadable videos (9,103 missing locally out of 21,083 WLASL instances).
  • Explicit recognition metrics (Top-1, Macro-F1, Confusion Matrix).
  • Excluded Approach:
  • End-to-end RGB I3D baseline: requires multi-GPU clusters and massive video storage unsuitable for real-time edge landmark processing.
  • Reusing original splits as the sole evaluation: original splits permit signer leakage; our primary benchmark mandates a strictly signer-independent split.
  • Validation Method:
  • Ingestion tests verifying gloss-to-ID mapping and missing video isolation without assigning false class 0.

docs.title: Reference B: SignBart
docs.text:
• Repository URL: https://github.com/TinhNguyen2312/SignBart
  • Inspected Files:
  • models/sign_bart.py: Skeleton sequence encoder and Bart-based representation.
  • datasets/preprocess.py: Landmark coordinate normalization and component separation.
  • configs/default.yaml: Modality configurations and ablation parameters.
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Highly relevant for isolated sign landmark representation: demonstrates that component-aware coordinate normalization (hands relative to wrist, body relative to shoulders) vastly outperforms unstructured vector flattening.
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • Structured 3D coordinate tensor [T, J, 3] with explicit landmark masks.
  • Modality separation: Left Hand (21), Right Hand (21), Pose (upper body joints), Face (lips/contours).
  • Normalization: anatomical centering per component; scale normalization by inter-shoulder distance or hand bounding box diagonal.
  • License & Restrictions:
  • MIT License.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Geometric coordinate normalization operating on 3D coordinates (N, 3) rather than flattened feature vectors.
  • Component-specific spatial projection encoders before temporal fusion.
  • Independent modality masking so missing hands or face do not pollute feature means.
  • Excluded Approach:
  • Full BART language model backbone: excessive compute overhead for isolated word classification; our research investigates real-time spatial-temporal fusion architectures.
  • Validation Method:
  • Unit tests verifying translation and scale invariance on 3D geometric coordinates with partial modality dropouts.

docs.title: Reference C: OpenHands
docs.text:
• Repository URL: https://github.com/AI4Bharat/openhands
  • Inspected Files:
  • openhands/models/pose/: Pose-based recognizers (SL-GCN, ST-GCN, HRNet).
  • openhands/apis/inference.py: Pose extraction and inference pipeline.
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Demonstrates spatial-temporal graph convolutions (ST-GCN / SL-GCN) on 2D/3D pose landmarks for sign language recognition.
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • Graph convolutional network using physical body/hand adjacency matrix.
  • Fixed landmark schemas and PyTorch Lightning-based experiment management.
  • License & Restrictions:
  • MIT License.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Modality graph grouping concepts (pose vs. left hand vs. right hand) and lightweight temporal pooling mechanisms.
  • Excluded Approach:
  • Wholesale external dependency on OpenHands package: introduces heavyweight conflicting dependency trees and rigid dataset format expectations.
  • Validation Method:
  • Native PyTorch baseline implementations (MLP, LSTM, GRU, Temporal Transformer) sharing identical tensor schemas and collators.

docs.title: Reference D: Real-Time Landmark-Based LSTM Implementation
docs.text:
• Repository URL: https://github.com/bNhN-0/asl-recognition-lstm
  • Inspected Files:
  • train.py: Sequence windowing and LSTM training.
  • app.py: OpenCV webcam loop and rolling buffer.
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Real-time webcam inference loop for word/gesture recognition using rolling temporal windows.
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • Rolling sequence buffer deque(maxlen=T) for webcam frames.
  • Prediction smoothing and confidence thresholding.
  • Label dictionary and normalization statistics saved alongside model weights.
  • License & Restrictions:
  • MIT License.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Requirement that training, offline evaluation, and webcam inference share identical versioned preprocessing pipelines, label encodings, and normalization statistics.
  • Real-time rolling buffer with confidence threshold gating.
  • Excluded Approach:
  • Replicating their specific dataset or presenting their numbers as WLASL baselines (their model is trained on a small private gesture set).
  • Validation Method:
  • End-to-end test verifying that feeding an identical sequence to offline evaluation and RealTimePredictor yields bitwise identical logits.

docs.title: Reference E: Runtime and Deployment Design (Sign-Language-Translator)
docs.text:
• Repository URL: https://github.com/Abdul-Nafee/Sign-Language-Translator
  • Inspected Files:
  • backend/app.py: Backend inference server.
  • frontend/: UI display, prediction debouncing, and latency measuring.
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Production-ready separation of frame capture, landmark extraction, and model inference.
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • Decoupled inference service loading model once at startup.
  • Prediction smoothing / debouncing to eliminate frame-to-frame flicker.
  • License & Restrictions:
  • MIT License.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Single predictor initialization on FastAPI startup (lifespan handler).
  • Debounce/smoother utility with configurable window.
  • Excluded Approach:
  • Full sentence generation / text-to-speech (out of scope for dynamic word-level classification).
  • Validation Method:
  • FastAPI tests validating startup model residency, health status, and batch prediction latency.

docs.title: Reference F: Official MediaPipe Tasks API
docs.text:
• Repository / Docs URL: https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/holistic_landmarker/python
  • Inspected Files / APIs:
  • mediapipe.tasks.python.vision.HolisticLandmarker
  • HolisticLandmarkerOptions, RunningMode.VIDEO, RunningMode.IMAGE
  • Model asset: holistic_landmarker.task (13.6 MB, located in models/mediapipe/)
  • Research / Task Match:
  • Canonical holistic feature extractor producing 553 landmarks:
    • Left Hand: 21 landmarks
    • Right Hand: 21 landmarks
    • Pose: 33 landmarks
    • Face: 478 landmarks
  • Architecture / Engineering Pattern:
  • Video processing mode requires monotonically increasing timestamps in milliseconds (detect_for_video(mp_image, timestamp_ms)).
  • Frames must be in SRGB format: OpenCV BGR frames require explicit cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB).
  • Reusing an initialized landmarker instance per worker thread to avoid heavy re-initialization.
  • Explicit resource release via .close().
  • License & Restrictions:
  • Apache 2.0 License.
  • Adopted Approach:
  • Proper color space conversion (BGR -> RGB).
  • Video mode with monotonic timestamping.
  • Worker-level landmarker reuse with graceful resource release.
  • Zero-placeholder for missing landmarks accompanied by an explicit boolean validity mask.
  • Excluded Approach:
  • Deprecated legacy mp.solutions.holistic pipeline.
  • Silently substituting zeros when the model asset is absent.
  • Validation Method:
  • Unit tests verifying BGR-to-RGB conversion, timestamp monotonicity, and landmarker resource lifecycle.
